cards.d: If someone is aggressive, then they constantly want to fight.
cards.e: Nobody liked to play games with him because he was always too aggressive.
cards.ielts: Experts disagree about whether violent video games make young people more aggressive in their behaviour towards others.

cards.d: Amnesty is a pardon given to prisoners of war.
cards.e: She was denied amnesty for her involvement in the war.
cards.ielts: The government offered an amnesty to anyone who handed in illegal weapons, and thousands of guns were collected within a month.

cards.d: An arena is a building where people can watch sports and concerts.
cards.e: The new arena was all set to hold the championship match.
cards.ielts: Hosting the Olympics often requires cities to build huge new arenas, which may remain empty once the games are over.

cards.d: An auditorium is a large building used for public events.
cards.e: People have gathered at the school auditorium to watch the play.
cards.ielts: The university auditorium was packed with students who had come to hear a famous scientist speak about artificial intelligence.

cards.d: A captive is a prisoner.
cards.e: The guards told the captive that there was no way he could escape the prison.
cards.ielts: Critics argue that zoos treat wild animals as captives, while supporters claim they protect endangered species from extinction.

cards.d: Combat is fighting between two people or groups.
cards.e: The two warriors were locked in combat.
cards.ielts: Many soldiers who have experienced combat suffer from mental health problems long after they return home from war.

cards.d: If something is commonplace, then it is ordinary.
cards.e: There is nothing commonplace about the way Morris dresses.
cards.ielts: Online banking, which seemed futuristic twenty years ago, has now become commonplace in almost every country in the world.

cards.d: A compound is an enclosed area such as a prison or factory.
cards.e: The workers waited outside the compound for the gates to the factory to open.
cards.ielts: The embassy staff lived inside a secure compound surrounded by high walls and guarded by soldiers day and night.

cards.d: A corps is a division of a military force.
cards.e: The army had a corps of archers who trained apart from the regular soldiers.
cards.ielts: The country’s medical corps was sent to the flooded region to treat injured residents and prevent the spread of disease.

cards.d: To distract someone means to stop them from concentrating on something.
cards.e: The phone call distracted him so much that he forgot all about his homework.
cards.ielts: Mobile phones in classrooms can easily distract students, so many schools have decided to ban them during lessons.

cards.d: If someone is dumb, they are unable to speak.
cards.e: She did not share the secret. She remained silent as if she were dumb.
cards.ielts: When the results were announced, I was struck dumb with surprise, because I had never expected to win the scholarship.

cards.d: A foe is an enemy or opponent.
cards.e: It was hard to believe that anyone could be his foe.
cards.ielts: The two countries, once bitter foes, have become close trading partners since signing a peace agreement in the 1990s.

cards.d: To hack something means to cut it into uneven pieces.
cards.e: My uncle used the ax to hack the tree into many logs.
cards.ielts: Illegal loggers hack down large areas of rainforest every year, destroying the habitats of countless endangered species.

cards.d: To meditate means to focus or think deeply in silence.
cards.e: She liked to meditate for several hours of each day.
cards.ielts: More companies are encouraging employees to meditate during breaks, as research shows it reduces stress and improves concentration.

cards.ru: слегка порезать; делать, с- зарубку на
cards.d: To nick someone means to cut them slightly with a sharp object.
cards.e: While cutting the carrots, the cook nicked his finger with the edge of his knife.
cards.ielts: While cooking dinner for my family, I accidentally nicked my thumb with a sharp knife, but luckily it was only a small cut.

cards.ru: сердить, рас-; выводить, вывести из себя
cards.d: To provoke someone means to annoy them on purpose to cause violence.
cards.e: The older boy provoked Paul by calling him mean names.
cards.ielts: Some football fans deliberately provoke supporters of rival teams, which can lead to violence outside stadiums.

cards.d: A realm is any area of activity or interest.
cards.e: He was not very active in the realm of business.
cards.ielts: Advances in the realm of medicine have increased life expectancy dramatically over the past century.

cards.d: A reign is the period of time in which a ruler rules.
cards.e: The emperor’s reign lasted for only two years.
cards.ielts: During the reign of Amir Temur, Samarkand became one of the most important centres of science and architecture in the world.

cards.d: Rust is a red and brown coating on iron objects caused by water and air.
cards.e: The old metal gate would not swing because the hinges were covered in rust.
cards.ielts: Old bridges in coastal cities need regular maintenance, as salty air causes rust to form on the steel much faster.

cards.d: If something is sacred, then it is worshipped and respected.
cards.e: One religion in India will not harm cows because it believes that they are sacred.
cards.ielts: Many ancient sites are sacred to local communities, so tourism there must be managed carefully to show respect for their beliefs.
